coaching.headline: Countess ran Greystone over and we took ten towers to their two. The only giveaway was a free Fangtooth.
coaching.team: A proper win built on structures, not a kill count. We won seven of eight fights, turned five of them into an objective or tower, and our base lost two outer towers and nothing else.

focus.title: No free Fangtooth
focus.evidence: Their first Fangtooth fell with all five of us alive and no fight recorded around it. The second fell while we took Orb Prime and their inhibitor, which is a trade worth making. The difference is whether we took something in return.
focus.action: Before each Fangtooth spawn, the jungler calls contest or trade. A trade names the tower or Prime we take at the same time; if nobody can name one, all five go to the pit. Next game, no enemy Fangtooth falls for nothing while all five of us are alive.

perPlayer.cae6a91f-44c7-4dea-9cad-b5c187c3988a: Countess was a fucking nightmare for Greystone: first blood, seven of his eight deaths, the biggest hero damage in the lobby and a single death all game. That is the standard. The next step is turning his deaths into structures. When Greystone goes down and a friendly wave is near his tower, Countess calls the push and hits it with the wave before hunting the next kill.
perPlayer.729c3aa1-206a-4fe5-bd0e-216cc0ce10f8: Renna owned Iggy & Scorch: all three of his deaths were hers, and three out of three is a pattern. When Renna is alive and her ultimate could be up, Iggy plants turrets and oil from behind Steel or Countess and holds Epoch for her burst. Credit where due: he hit harder than his usual pace and left the second-highest objective damage on the team, which a zone mage should.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Rampage killed Murdock and Wukong made him pay for it. Goldilocks finished with no deaths, the team's heaviest objective damage and two kills on Rampage inside fights we won. Keep that punish: whenever Rampage commits onto a carry, Wukong follows him in and finishes him.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 ran the standard core, beat his usual damage pace and outdamaged Sparrow. The problem is the order of deaths. Murdock went down first in two teamfights, both times to Sparrow, and being her opening snack twice is a shit habit. When Sparrow is alive as a fight starts, Murdock drops a trap in front of himself, shoots from behind Steel, and saves Pacifier for the exit until she commits.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy's Steel did the support job properly, and the next layer is a Sparrow peel plan: once she starts shooting, Steel drops Force Shield between her arrows and Murdock and saves Shield Bash for when she commits. Twenty wards to Phase's nine, the most mitigation on our team, and one death, in our only lost fight right after Sparrow killed Murdock.

15.9.call: We won the kill sequence 3-0, yet our Outer Tower fell in the same window, shortly after Renna killed Iggy & Scorch in a separate exchange. The kills did not save the structure; which lane it was is not recorded.

19.5.call: Our only lost fight, 2-3, with Murdock and then Steel the first deaths. Mini Prime was already ours and Fangtooth followed shortly after, so the window still paid out despite the bodies.

22.2.call: Won 3-1 and their Inner Tower followed. Wukong killed Rampage right after Rampage took Murdock down, so the exchange ended in our favor before the tower fell; the timing does not show who took the tower.

26.1.call: Won 3-2 as their inhibitor fell, while they took Fangtooth in the same window. Orb Prime had already fallen to us; the timing does not show who was at the pit.

matchup: Countess dominated Greystone: seven of his eight deaths were credited to her.
Greystone's Tainted Bastion cuts healing on magical attackers, hitting both her damage and much of her sustain.
Renna brings the heaviest magical damage, Phase the enemy healing.
build: Megacosm's burn scales off the bonus health Greystone's Overlord and Augmentation supply.
Caustica punishes bonus magical armor such as Tainted Bastion or Rampage's Void Helm while targets are above half health.
eternal: Vesh, Lich and Mind Rot fit a hero who lands repeated ability hits and heals off them.
Tithe of Death is the first-minor alternative for a high-kill pace, giving up Lich's steady sustain.
augment: Sanguine Slash makes Blade Siphon hit harder and heal more against isolated targets, suiting a lone offlaner.
Shadow Strike is the swap if getting Shadow Slip back sooner matters more than that damage.
crest: Tempest pulses magical damage into nearby heroes and heals off it, with repeat hits reduced.
It pays inside two or three enemies, matching her dive role; this is fit rather than proof.
improvement: Keep the damage-and-sustain package; one death does not argue for a swap.
If Sparrow or Rampage start finishing her in long fights, Golem's Gift adds physical armor over a late damage slot.
The missing physical armor is a draft-level warning here, not a proven cost.

matchup: Renna, the enemy's heaviest damage dealer, was credited with all three of his deaths.
Her Wraith Leggings and Overseer make a low-health Iggy the easy target.
Rampage and Greystone are bulky bodies for his burn zones; Phase and Rampage's healing made anti-heal relevant.
build: Megacosm and Entropy are the burn core; Noxia rewards following one ability's mark with a different ability.
Tainted Scepter was the only anti-heal item on our team, with Phase and Rampage both healing.
It replaces Orb Of Growth's bonus experience and cast healing.
eternal: Vesh suits fire zones, since repeated ability ticks feed its damage-over-time echo.
Mind Rot adds damage strongest at the start of a fight; Lich gives lane sustain.
Phylactery is the second-minor alternative if Renna's burst keeps ending him, at the cost of Mind Rot's damage.
augment: Hold This! permanently grows Molotov's explosion damage each time it hits a hero.
Turret Maniac is the alternative for objective zone control, trading turret health for a fourth turret.
crest: Epoch's stasis is the main tool for waiting out Renna's pull, ultimate zone and burst.
The record does not show whether it was used before the three deaths; fit, not proof.
improvement: If Renna keeps finding him, Spellbreaker is the conditional swap, giving up Megacosm's burn.
Spellbreaker adds magical armor and a spell shield that blocks one ability.
Keep Tainted Scepter while Phase and Rampage are the healers the team needs to cut.

matchup: Rampage did the most healing in the lobby but got one kill all game.
Wukong killed him twice inside fights we won and never died.
Sparrow and Renna are the fragile gank targets; Greystone and Phase are poorer uses of a gank.
build: Infernum hits harder into the bonus armor from Rampage's Elafrost; The Perforator ignores armor and slows.
Skipping Syonic Echo trades its post-cast attack-speed bursts for that armor penetration.
eternal: Lotus grants small random bonuses; Early Bloom adds an extra level.
Immaculate protects the opening of a fight, only while Wukong is near full health.
Masterpiece is the aggressive alternative, trading a guaranteed level for value that only pays when kills come.
augment: Masterful Mimicry raises the clone cap by one and generates Hair, fitting the stance-and-clone plan.
From Up High is the alternative only for a plan built around leap damage from height.
crest: Nex stores damage dealt to heroes, then dashes and releases it as a burst with a short slow.
It rewards trading first and finishing second, useful against Rampage once he is low.
improvement: Keep the current build for now: Wukong killed Rampage twice and never died.
If Rampage's sustain starts winning jungle fights, Tainted Trident adds anti-heal over The Perforator's penetration and slow.

matchup: Sparrow's three kills all landed on our duo, two on Murdock, who has no dash.
Phase built damage items, not a protective core, so the enemy duo threatened burst.
Rampage's Elafrost was the only completed physical-armor item on their team.
build: The common carry core with nothing off-script, so there is no build deviation to explain.
eternal: Vermis adds maximum-health damage on every third consecutive basic attack, and Serration adds missing-health damage to that hit.
Melting Point only adds damage against very high physical armor, and only Rampage carried a physical-armor item.
Sub-Surface is the second-minor alternative, cutting damage from Renna's zones and Sparrow's arrow volley at the cost of Melting Point's high-armor bonus.
augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired pierce and reach further, past minions or frontline to Sparrow or Renna.
Sting Operation is the swap if more traps for self-peel matter more than reach.
crest: Pacifier is the immobile carry's main repositioning tool as well as a finisher.
Spending it forward removes the exit against Sparrow or Rampage.
improvement: If Rampage's or Phase's healing keeps the target alive, Tainted Rounds adds anti-heal, giving up Imperator's critical-damage boost.
Iggy's scepter was the only anti-heal and only works when his magical damage hits that same target.

matchup: Phase ran damage items rather than a protective core, so her threat was poke and healing.
Renna was the heaviest damage dealer, and it was magical; Rampage did the most healing.
Steel's own kills on Phase and Sparrow show the duo pressure went both ways.
build: Dynamo pairs with Shield Bash and the ultimate stun; Xenia shields nearby allies and adds both armors.
Fire Blossom takes the place of Gaia Greaves from the common core.
eternal: Krix adds health; Feeding Frenzy speeds Heavy Metal's empowered punches in crowded fights.
Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue when anti-heal is short, costing recovery between trades.
augment: Heavy Metal adds damage based on total armor, and Fire Blossom, Dynamo and Xenia all feed it.
That is how a tank build keeps threatening damage.
crest: Tranquility heals nearby allies and raises the ward cap.
Twenty wards to Phase's nine shows the vision tools were used heavily; ward locations are not recorded.
improvement: Keep the current package while Sparrow's and Rampage's physical damage is the main problem.
If Renna's or Phase's magical damage becomes the main threat, Tainted Bastion adds magical armor and anti-heal over Raiment.
One death all match does not demand a swap.

threats: Heal-stacking: Phase. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 1 item of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ultPlus: Overseer (Exalted): Enhance your Ultimate Ability: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,269 hero damage a minute, more than 81% of Renna mid players this patch (35% of the team's). The damage came from Entropy, Noxia, Overseer.
Abyssal Rift at rank 3: 95s base, about 66.4s by the end (30% shorter) from 43 ability haste: Entropy 15, Noxia 20, Epoch 8.
Overseer (Exalted): Enhance your Ultimate Ability: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Renna dealt 39,339 hero damage, 35% of their team's, with +375 magical power from items.

Penetration: Overseer 8, Wraith Leggings 11; against Iggy & Scorch (level 17: about 47 magical armor, 28 after penetration; took 9,282 magical damage from heroes, 49% of all hero damage they took) and Murdock (level 16: about 45 magical armor, 26 after penetration; took 7,376 magical damage from heroes, 54% of all hero damage they took) that is about 15% and 15% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Entropy (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 3 (+3.5%) additional Damage. Each Ability can only trigger this effect once every 0.2s, per Target.
Noxia (item): Deal 6% of Target's Maximum Health as bonus Damage.
Overseer (item): Ultimate: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Vesh (Eternal): Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% a minute, about 19.4% by the end) of that damage as a DoT over 3s.
Millennia (Eternal minor): Every 60s, increase your Ultimate Ability Damage by 0.75%.

Sustain: 7% magical lifesteal; Overseer: Ultimate: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.; Lich: Gain 4%/7%/10%/14% Magical Lifesteal at Levels 1/6/11/16.; 3,519 healing recorded.

Lesson: Renna's penetration cut through: Iggy & Scorch took about 15% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 17 their armor was about 47, about 28 after 19 flat penetration).

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Entropy, Noxia, Wraith Leggings, Vesh. Renna has 4 damaging abilities (Stupor hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 43 ability haste brought them back 30% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Overseer, Lich.
The Eternal was part of it: Vesh (Lich + Millennia) sits on the same triggers as the items (every ability hit set off; healing off the damage), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 0 of the 1 players Renna killed built magical armor. Anti-heal on Iggy & Scorch. We killed Renna 4 times.
Copy it? Vesh (Lich + Millennia): 51.5% in 3,660 Renna midlane games, level with the hero's 52.2%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

card.lesson: Abyssal Rift came back about every 66s instead of 95s by the end (30% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.

ultPlus: Timewarp (Chime): Every 8s: Subtract 1s from Non-Ultimate Cooldowns.
Overseer (Exalted): Enhance your Ultimate Ability: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 2,493 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Countess offlane players this patch (43% of the team's). The damage came from Megacosm, Caustica, Overseer.
Feast at rank 3: 85s base, about 53.8s by the end (37% shorter) from 58 ability haste: Timewarp 25, Megacosm 10, Lifebinder 15, Tempest 8.
Timewarp (Chime): Every 8s: Subtract 1s from Non-Ultimate Cooldowns.
Overseer (Exalted): Enhance your Ultimate Ability: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Countess dealt 77,269 hero damage, 43% of their team's, with +530 magical power from items.

Penetration: Overseer 8, Caustica ignores 35%; against Greystone (level 16: about 103 magical armor, 59 after penetration; took 36,265 magical damage from heroes, 68% of all hero damage they took) and Phase (level 15: about 44 magical armor, 21 after penetration; took 15,020 magical damage from heroes, 68% of all hero damage they took) that is about 28% and 19% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 2.5% of Target's Max Health as Damage over 3s. Additional applications refresh the duration.
Megacosm (item): On dealing Ability Damage to Heroes: Deal 6% of Target's Bonus Health as Damage over 3s.
Caustica (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Hero: While they are above 50% Health. For every point of Bonus Magical Armor they possess. Deal 0.2% more Damage.
Overseer (item): Ultimate: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.
Tempest (crest): Deal 15 (+15%) Damage to 3 nearby Heroes every second for 7s. Heal equal to 35% of the damage dealt. Additional hits against the same Target deal 20% Damage.
Vesh (Eternal): Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% a minute, about 19.4% by the end) of that damage as a DoT over 3s.
Mind Rot (Eternal minor): The major also deals 2% of the target's current health as bonus damage.
Sanguine Slash (augment): Blade Siphon deals 20% more damage and heals 50% more against Isolated Targets.

Sustain: 19% magical lifesteal; Overseer: Ultimate: Deals 15% more damage. Heals you for 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes.; Tempest: Deal 15 (+15%) Damage to 3 nearby Heroes every second for 7s. Heal equal to 35% of the damage dealt. Additional hits against the same Target deal 20% Damage.; Lich: Gain 4%/7%/10%/14% Magical Lifesteal at Levels 1/6/11/16.; 19,689 healing recorded.
Toughness: +350 health; took 53,566 damage, mitigated 32,831, died 1 times.

Lesson: Countess's penetration cut through: Greystone took about 28% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 16 their armor was about 103, about 59 after 8 flat + 35% penetration).

Loadout augment Sanguine Slash: Blade Siphon deals 20% more damage and heals 50% more against Isolated Targets. (changes Blade Siphon, 4.4s cooldown with their haste) Field: 48.9% in 712 games, 49% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.2%.

Loadout Eternal Vesh: Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% per minute) of that damage as a DoT over 3s. [7% growing 0.4% a minute: about 19.4% by the end (31 min)] Field: 51.2% in 787 games, 55% of picks, level the hero-role's 51.2%.
Loadout minor Lich: Gain 4%/7%/10%/14% Magical Lifesteal at Levels 1/6/11/16. Field: 50.9% in 713 games, 91% of picks, level the hero-role's 51.2%.
Loadout minor Mind Rot: The major also deals 2% of the target's current health as bonus damage. Field: 54.7% in 300 games, 38% of picks, above the hero-role's 51.2%.

Loadout crest Tempest: Overcharge:  Deal 15 (+15%) Damage to 3 nearby Heroes every second for 7s. Heal equal to 35% of the damage dealt. Additional hits against the same Target deal 20% Damage. Field: 48.1% in 565 games, 39% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.2%.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 5 effects on one trigger: Overseer, Lifebinder, Tempest, Lich, Sanguine Slash.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Caustica, Vesh, Mind Rot. Countess has 4 damaging abilities (Blade Siphon, Shadow Slip, Eventide hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 58 ability haste brought them back 37% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Damage that scales with our health): 2 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Mind Rot. The more health a target stacks, the more these deal, so health items on our side fed them.

The Eternal was part of it: Vesh (Lich + Mind Rot) sits on the same triggers as the items (healing off the damage; every ability hit set off; damage that scales with our health), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 3 players Countess killed built magical armor (Greystone). Anti-heal on Greystone. We killed Countess 1 time.
Copy it? Vesh (Lich + Mind Rot): 55.5% in 281 Countess offlane games, above the hero's 51.2%. Proven this patch: worth copying.

card.lesson: Feast came back about every 54s instead of 85s by the end (37% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.
